stranger.en: It's a social media trend where people record themselves talking to strangers and sometimes being rejected.
stranger.zh: 这是一种社交媒体潮流，人们会录下自己与陌生人搭话，有时还会被拒绝的过程。

stranger.en: Hannah says that when she walked up to the first stranger in the video, she felt her adrenaline spiking.
stranger.zh: Hannah 说，当她在视频中走向第一个陌生人时，她感到肾上腺素飙升（spiking）。

step.en: And the second is that governments are now stepping in to help the financing of new nuclear power stations, guaranteeing the price for a set period, or offering a more manageable interest rate .
step.zh: 第二，各国政府现在正在介入以协助新核电站的融资，在一定期限内对电价进行托底，或提供更易承受的利率。

step.en: And so, I wonder whether that might make people more shy of speaking to strangers – worried that the people will, you know, not appraise them in a good way, and so doing something like this to try to counter that might feel like a positive step to people, that they're trying to do something.
step.zh: 所以我在想，这是否会让大家更羞于与陌生人交谈——担心别人对自己的评价不高。因此，通过做这样的事情来对抗这种心理，大家可能会觉得是一种积极的尝试，至少说明他们在做出努力。

strategic.en: To quote him exactly, "It was a serious strategic mistake to exit nuclear energy… we simply don’t have enough energy generation capacity ."
strategic.zh: 原话是这样说的：“退出核能是一个严重的战略错误……我们根本没有足够的发电能力。”

steady.en: Grid engineers call this baseload power : a steady, reliable supply that is always there, whatever the weather.
steady.zh: 电网工程师称之为“基荷电力”：一种无论天气如何，始终稳定、可靠的供应。

steady.en: And increasingly, governments have concluded that nuclear and renewables need to work together, with nuclear providing the steady backbone that a renewable -heavy grid needs to actually function.
steady.zh: 越来越多的政府得出结论：核能和可再生能源需要协同工作，由核能提供稳定的骨干支撑，以使依赖可再生能源的电网能够真正运转。

strategy.en: In Finland, the Green party voted back in 2022 to formally support nuclear power as part of its climate strategy, and the tone has started to change in several other countries too.
strategy.zh: 早在2022年，芬兰绿党就投票正式支持将核能作为其气候战略的一部分，其他几个国家的态度也开始发生转变。

state.en: Data centres in the United States now use more than 4% of the country's entire electricity supply.
state.zh: 美国的数据中心目前消耗了该国全社会用电量的4%以上。

state.en: Take the United States. Pizza is very strongly associated with New York food culture, even though pizza is an Italian food, originated in Italy.
state.zh: 以美国为例。披萨与纽约饮食文化紧密相连，尽管披萨是意大利食物，起源于意大利。

state.en: Add it all together, and the nuclear capacity now committed to data centres by these companies is up to 13 gigawatts , and that is just in the United States.
state.zh: 总而言之，这些公司目前承诺为数据中心提供的核电容量已高达13吉瓦，而这仅仅是在美国。

steadily.en: And for most of the last twenty years, these buildings have been growing steadily but predictably.
steadily.zh: 在过去二十年的大部分时间里，这些建筑一直在稳定但可预测地增长。

stretch.en: There are long waiting lists to ensure that a new customer won't overload the local network, and in some parts of the United States, these waiting lists stretch to eight years, which is eight years too long if you're a technology company racing to build the next generation of AI.
stretch.zh: 排队等待的名单很长，以确保新客户不会使当地网络过载，而在美国某些地区，排队时间长达八年，对于一家竞相开发下一代人工智能的科技公司来说，八年实在太漫长了。

stage.en: And here, enter stage right , nuclear power.
It is in the final stages of opening a nuclear storage site deep underground that will be able to safely store nuclear waste for 100,000 years.
stage.zh: 它在地下深处建造的核废料处置库已处于最后开放阶段，该处置库将能安全储存核废料长达10万年。

storage.en: It is in the final stages of opening a nuclear storage site deep underground that will be able to safely store nuclear waste for 100,000 years.
storage.zh: 它在地下深处建造的核废料处置库已处于最后开放阶段，该处置库将能安全储存核废料长达10万年。

stereotype.en: And this is actually partly where the stereotype of British food becoming bad comes from.
stereotype.zh: 这也是英国食物变坏的刻板印象部分来源。

stereotype.en: This stereotype is not completely new. British people themselves have made jokes about their country’s food for years.
stereotype.zh: 这种刻板印象并非完全新鲜。英国人自己多年来一直拿他们国家的食物开玩笑。

stew.en: Pies and stews, puddings, and dishes that could feed an entire family.
stew.zh: 馅饼和炖菜、布丁，以及能养活一整个家庭的菜肴。

stew.en: A common meal might be a type of vegetable stew called pottage .
stew.zh: 一顿普通的饭菜可能是一种叫做pottage的蔬菜炖菜。

status.en: They were really expensive, so they were associated with wealth and status, but they were used generously .
status.zh: 它们真的很昂贵，因此它们与财富和地位联系在一起，但它们的使用毫不吝啬。

style.en: British curry houses develop their own styles of curries and their own sauces and breads that aren’t really found in South Asia.
style.zh: 英国的咖喱屋开发了他们自己风格的咖喱以及在南亚并不常见的自己的酱汁和面包。

style.en: Italian immigrants moved to the US, transformed the dish pizza to a new style, created New York and Chicago pizzas that are now distinctly American.
style.zh: 意大利移民搬到美国，将披萨这道菜转变为一种新的风格，创造了现在明显具有美国特色的纽约和芝加哥披萨。

strongly.en: Take the United States. Pizza is very strongly associated with New York food culture, even though pizza is an Italian food, originated in Italy.
strongly.zh: 以美国为例。披萨与纽约饮食文化紧密相连，尽管披萨是意大利食物，起源于意大利。

sticky.en: A well-made sticky toffee pudding is perhaps the best dessert in the world, in my opinion.
sticky.zh: 在我看来，一个制作精良的太妃糖布丁也许是世界上最好的甜点。

sticky.en: British food also has lots of desserts and cakes: sticky toffee pudding, Eton mess, bread and butter pudding.
sticky.zh: 英国食物也有很多甜点和蛋糕：太妃糖布丁、伊顿混乱、面包黄油布丁。

steak.en: A steak and ale pie or a shepherd’s pie or a Cornish pasty are great.
steak.zh: 牛排艾尔馅饼、牧羊人馅饼或康沃尔肉馅饼都很棒。
